title: Tenant Data Governance and Access Forensics Guide
author: Priya N. Patel
content:
Overview

This guide defines the end-to-end controls and operational steps for tenant-level data governance, access forensics, and compliance evidence collection at Redwood Inference. It bridges RBAC configuration, audit-log model, retention mappings, secure-SDLC touchpoints for access changes, and incident response steps for multi-tenant access anomalies. The intended audience is Security, SRE, Platform, and Private Deployments teams.

Goals
- Ensure we can reconstruct who accessed which tenant data, when, and from where, within required legal and contractual windows.
- Standardize evidence packaging for regulatory, enterprise, and internal investigations.
- Define acceptable retention windows and escalation patterns for exceptions.

Scope
- Applies to all hosted and dedicated tenant traffic handled by Redwood inference runtime and control plane.
- Includes: control-plane RBAC events, inference request metadata (non-content traces), audit logs, key rotation records, and tenant residency tags.
- Excludes raw model weights and ephemeral GPU memory dumps except where forensics requires preserved dumps under legal hold process.

Ownership & Roles
- Data Governance Owner: Leah Kim (Security PM) — policy decisions, legal coordination.
- Forensics Lead: Marco Ruiz (SRE/Forensics) — evidence collection, chain-of-custody.
- RBAC Owner: Anil Suresh (Identity & Access Eng) — role definitions and provisioning flows.
- Incident Commander: assigned per incident via normal incident rota.

Key Concepts and Definitions
- Tenant ID: canonical internal tenant identifier (ten-<4hex>).
- Access Event: any control-plane or data-plane request that results in authentication and an authorization decision.
- Evidence Bundle: time-bounded set of logs, artifacts, and provenance metadata packaged for audit.
- Residency Tag: region/geo marker attached to tenant metadata for retention policy decisions.

High-level Requirements
1) Unambiguous linkage: Every access event must include tenant_id, actor_id (service or user), authz_decision, auth_method, source_ip, user_agent, and request_id.
2) Immutable audit chain: Control-plane events must be written to an immutable audit store supporting append-only retention and signed manifests.
3) Retention alignment: Retention windows must be derived from the tenant residency_tag and contract (see retention table below).
4) Forensic readiness: Snapshot hooks for checkpointing KV caches, ephemeral ingress traces, and model-serving traces on suspected exfil events.

Audit Data Model (example canonical event)
- timestamp: 2026-11-03T14:22:33Z
- tenant_id: ten-1a2b
- actor_id: svc-ingress-proxy-3
- principal_type: service_account | user | api_key
- authn_method: OIDC | mTLS | API_KEY
- authz_decision: ALLOW | DENY | Fallback-Policy-Triggered
- resource_path: /v1/generate
- request_id: rc-9f3a
- source_ip: 18.205.12.40
- user_agent: Redwood-API-Client/2.1
- additional_metadata: residency=eu-west-1; container=runtime-a

(Above is an illustrative flattened JSON used in logs; actual event records are newline-delimited JSON written to the audit topic.)

Retention Mapping Table (policy summary)
- Tenant residency: EU (gdpr-relevant) => Audit events: 7 years; Control-plane manifests: 7 years; Forensic snapshots (by exception): 7 years.
- Tenant residency: US-only => Audit events: 3 years; manifests: 3 years; Forensic snapshots: 3 years.
- Tenant residency: APAC => Audit events: 5 years; manifests: 5 years; Forensic snapshots: 5 years.
- System service accounts and infra-level traces: 1 year (unless tied to a tenant investigation).

Retention decision flow (numbered procedure)
1. On tenant creation/update, set residency_tag from the customer profile and contract. Owner: Customer Onboarding team.
2. Map residency_tag to retention_profile via retention service (retention-service/v1/mapping).
3. Retention service enforces TTL on inactive audit topics and snapshot storage.
4. For exceptions, follow Risk & Exceptions special approvals (see section).

RBAC & Auth Controls
- Principle: Role-first minimal privilege. Roles are namespaced by product surface: control-plane: admin, auditor, operator; data-plane: inference-invoker, model-uploader (limited).
- Entitlements are implemented using XACML-inspired policies stored in the policy-store service. Policy versions are immutable and signed.
- API keys are short-lived by default (90 days) and support rotation via the key-manager. Service identities should prefer workload certificates (mTLS).

Example RBAC change lifecycle (developer-friendly)
1. Developer opens PR against infra-policy-repo to add a role binding.
2. CI verifies change against least-privilege linter and references required JIRA.
3. Change is deployed to staging policy-store and exercised by test harness.
4. After 48-hour canary, change is promoted to prod using blue/green policy rollout.

Audit Logging Architecture and Sources
- Primary sources: control-plane events (policy-store, authn-service), data-plane access logs (ingress-proxy), scheduler and orchestration traces, key-manager events, and KMS/HSM access logs.
- Ingestion path: sources -> kafka-audit-topic -> immutable-audit-archive (S3 with object-lock) -> cold-storage (regional) per retention profile.
- Integrity: Each daily shard has an HMAC manifest recorded in the manifest-catalog service and optionally notarized via signing key (HSM).

Forensics Playbook: Evidence Collection (step-by-step)
1. Triage: For any suspected tenant access anomaly, open an incident and tag it with tenant_id and evidence_tier (1=urgent, 2=standard).
2. Freeze window: For tier 1 incidents, retention-service marks related audit shards as legal-hold (no expiry) and notifies storage-owner.
3. Snapshot: Trigger runtime snapshot hook for the affected serving pool (command below).
   - Example CLI: redwood-forensics snapshot create --tenant ten-1a2b --pool runtime-a --reason "suspected-exfil" --initiator marco.ruiz@redwood.ai
4. Collect control-plane manifests for the 72-hour window around the event and verify HMAC chain.
5. Collate logs: Pull NDJSON from audit archive for the tenant_id and time window, compress to evidence bundle.
6. Preserve chain-of-custody: Record who exported the bundle, the export hash (SHA256), and store manifest in case-management system (e.g., CASE-12345).
7. If required, handoff to Legal for subpoenas or external counsel.

Evidence Bundle Contents (required)
- Audit NDJSON (access events) covering +/- 72 hours.
- Control-plane manifest (signed).
- Snapshot artifacts (if created): runtime snapshot metadata, storage locations, snapshot-hash.
- RBAC policy versions for any roles referenced in events.
- KMS audit snippet for key retrievals correlated to request_ids.
- Chain-of-custody log (who, when, why, hash).

Chain-of-Custody Template (text)
- Exported-by: marco.ruiz@redwood.ai
- Export-timestamp: 2026-11-03T15:02:12Z
- Evidence-hash: sha256:3a9f...
- Storage-path: s3://immutable-evidence/case-12345/
- Legal-hold: true

Query Recipes and Investigator Tools
- Quick query to isolate cross-tenant access via service-account:
  curl -s \\n    "https://audit-api.redwood.internal/v1/search?query=actor_id:%22svc-auth-proxy*%22%20AND%20tenant_id:%22ten-1a2b%22&start=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z&end=2026-11-04T00:00:00Z" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $FOR_EVIDENCE_TOKEN"

- Example Splunk/Kusto query (illustrative):
  index=audit tenant_id=ten-1a2b | where authz_decision!="DENY" | stats count() by actor_id, authn_method, day

Compliance Evidence Workflows (packaging for auditors)
1. Request intake: Compliance requests routed via compliance-requests@redwood.ai. Triage owner assigns priority and required scope.
2. Evidence scope agreed with requester, including time window, tenant_id, and retention restrictions.
3. Forensic collection executed per playbook. Evidence bundle is signed and delivered via secure transfer (SFTP or customer portal link).
4. Delivery record and receipt confirmation stored in the evidence catalog.

Risk & Exceptions Process (concise)
- Exception types: retention reduction, extended privileged access, cross-region log replication bypass.
- Approval path: Exception request -> Security Reviewer -> Legal (if data residency affected) -> Security Director -> Audit log of approval stored.
- Exceptions must include compensating controls, expiration date, and evidence that rollback is possible.

Required SLOs and Thresholds
- Audit ingestion latency: 99% of control-plane events must be ingested and durably stored within 30s of generation.
- Manifest signing: Daily manifest must be published within 1 hour of shard closure.
- Legal hold response: Initial legal-hold activation within 2 hours of a tier-1 request.

Operational Play: Example Incident Scenario
1. Detection: Automated anomaly detector flags unusual bulk token usage against tenant ten-1a2b. Alert page created and severity=P1.
2. Triage: Incident Commander assigns Forensics Lead and freezes affected shards.
3. Evidence collection: Snapshot and evidence bundle created per playbook.
4. App-level mitigation: Apply per-tenant throttling and rotate tenant API credentials.
5. Post-incident: Produce a forensics report, retention of evidence per residency mapping, and a blameless incident review with required follow-ups for RBAC policy gaps.

Audit & Review Cadence
- Quarterly tabletop exercises involving Legal, Security, Platform, and SRE for tenant-level incidents.
- Annual retention mapping review with Product & Finance.
- After-action: Every forensics response requires a 30-day remediation plan tracked in the security backlog.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Useful endpoints and service owners
  - audit-api: audit-api.redwood.internal (owner: Marco Ruiz)
  - retention-service: retention.redwood.internal (owner: Leah Kim)
  - manifest-catalog: manifest.redwood.internal (owner: Anil Suresh)

- Appendix B: Example legal-hold request template (email)
  Subject: Legal Hold Request - Case CASE-12345 - tenant ten-1a2b
  Body: Please place all audit shards and forensic snapshots related to tenant ten-1a2b on legal hold effective immediately. Reason: subpoena. Initiator: legal@redwood.ai

- Appendix C: Quick checklist for engineers exporting evidence
  - Confirm tenant_id and time window.
  - Verify HMAC chain on daily manifests.
  - Generate SHA256 on bundle and record chain-of-custody.
  - Notify Forensics Lead and Legal (if applicable).
